_note: One terabyte of traffic, priced by WHERE it goes rather than how much there is. The volume is held constant on purpose: the whole question is whether the destination changes the price, so the destination is the only thing allowed to vary. Written before any rate was looked up.
name: One terabyte of traffic, five destinations

paths.label: To the internet, via NAT Gateway

assumptions: Egress only where the provider bills egress; cross-AZ is billed in BOTH directions and both sides are counted, because both appear on the same account's bill.
AWS's 100 GB per month free internet egress allowance is applied once, to the internet paths.
One NAT Gateway in one AZ. A real multi-AZ setup needs one per AZ and the fixed cost multiplies; that is reported, not folded into the headline.
No Transit Gateway, no VPC peering across accounts, no PrivateLink interface endpoints. Each of those adds another per-GB charge and is out of scope.
List prices, on-demand, no committed-use discount.
